messages:
acme_ops: Hey @redwood-support — we have a customer ask: retroactive deletion for EU user data in project 'acme-prod' covering 2028-02-01 to 2028-02-28. They want DPA-compliant erasure and proof. They believe some requests may have been cached / left in backups. Ticket #7891.

zoe_support: Thanks @acme_ops — can you share affected customer_id(s) and a few sample request ids? Also, do they want export of deleted records + signed attestation or just deletion confirmation?

acme_ops: customer_id: acme-9876; sample_request: req_20280217_4432. They want export + audit logs showing deletion timeline + KMS key rotation/deletion details if relevant.

marco_security: Assigning security triage. @zoe_support, is this tenant hosted or on a private deployment? Need scope: app-layer vs snapshots in object storage.

zoe_support: Hosted in eu-west-1. No private deployment. I suspect snapshots/backups in S3. Checking retention policies now.

alan_eng: Quick question: do they require logical deletion only (app-level row deletion) or cryptographic erasure (KMS revoke/rotate so ciphertext is irrecoverable)? Both have different timelines.

priya_legal: Under the DPA they requested 'irreversible' erasure for EU data. We should present both options and ask customer to confirm which they accept. Also document scope in writing.

acme_ops: Customer says persistent backups must be included; they want proof of deletion of backups or proof of key destruction/rotation sufficient to render backups unreadable.

marco_security: For hosted customers we generally do one of: (1) identify snapshots encrypted with a dedicated KMS key and drive cryptographic erasure by rotating/deleting key material, or (2) identify and delete snapshots/objects in cloud provider if within retention policy. I need snapshot ARNs and KMS key IDs.

zoe_support: Pulling snapshot list from backup service. Will PM full output to security. Minimal redacted output here: 
```
backup_id: bk_20280217_01, s3_path: s3://redwood-backups/eu/bk_20280217_01, kms_key: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01
backup_id: bk_20280220_02, s3_path: s3://redwood-backups/eu/bk_20280220_02, kms_key: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01
```

marco_security: KMS key looks shared across those backups. Need to confirm whether key is customer-managed (in their AWS account) or Redwood-managed. If customer-managed, we advise steps; if Redwood-managed we can perform rotation and deletion.

zoe_support: Confirmed: key is Redwood-managed. (Verified with infra).

marco_security: Plan proposal:
1) Run application-layer erasure pipeline to remove tenant rows/objects.
2) Rotate the Redwood-managed KMS key and schedule secure deletion. Provide immutable audit logs of rotation and deletion scheduling.
3) Expire/overwrite backup objects per secure-delete policy and update manifest.
I'll coordinate with infra and give ETA.

acme_ops: Customer also requires audit-log snippets showing timeline of each deletion step. Can we provide replayable log lines with signatures or hashes?

alan_eng: We'll export audit logs for the tenant window. Command we use internally: 
```
rlog export --tenant acme-9876 --from 2028-02-28T00:00:00Z --to 2028-03-05T00:00:00Z --format jsonl
```
The export will include deletion API calls from 'erasure-runner' and KMS rotate events. We'll redact unrelated PII.

priya_legal: Keep chain-of-custody notes. We'll prepare a short attestation: scope, time, artifacts, and acceptance steps. Customer signature required.

zoe_support: ETA: I can run the app-layer erasure job by EOD tomorrow (2028-03-18). Marco, can infra queue KMS rotation + schedule key deletion window? Need to confirm provider hold periods.

marco_security: We can initiate rotation immediately and schedule deletion per cloud provider constraints. For an immediate attestation we can provide the rotation event + immutable audit log. For actual irreversible deletion (key material destruction) some providers have N-day deletion windows; I'm checking with infra.

alan_eng: Did a dry-run and captured sample log lines: 
```
2028-03-18T09:12:01Z erasure-runner DELETE /v1/project/acme-prod/data req=req_20280217_4432 status=200 actor=system
2028-03-18T09:12:03Z kms RotateKey key=arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01 actor=infra service=kms
2028-03-18T09:12:10Z backup-manager ExpireObject path=s3://redwood-backups/eu/bk_20280217_01 actor=backup-manager
```
I'll push full export to the secure channel when ready.

zoe_support: :thumbsup: I'll ask the customer to confirm they accept cryptographic erasure via key rotation+deletion as equivalent to physical blob deletion, or if they require provider-level snapshot removals.

acme_ops: They accept cryptographic erasure but demand explicit proof of key destruction. Also need list of sub-processors who might have had access to backups during that window.

marco_security: Sub-processor list (prelim): AWS (S3, KMS endpoints), internal backup-manager service, Redwood employees with admin roles. I'll produce a CSV with names/roles.

priya_legal: We'll collect signed confirmation and prepare any DPA amendment if required. Also request export of sub-processor access logs for the timeframe.

zoe_support: Next steps for customer (summary):
- Run app-layer deletion for tenant acme-9876 (EOD 2028-03-18).
- Rotate and schedule deletion of the Redwood-managed KMS key used for those backups.
- Export audit logs and redacted backup manifests; provide signed attestation.
- Include sub-processor list and access logs.
I'll update ticket #7891 with artifacts and timeline.

acme_ops: Please ensure timestamps are in UTC and include SHA256 of exported manifests and logs.

alan_eng: Will include hashes. Sample here: 
```
sha256sum backups_manifest.jsonl -> 9b1d3c2a5f...
sha256sum audit_export.jsonl -> a3f0c1b7d...
```

marco_security: I'll own the attestation text and sign it with our security key. @priya_legal once you confirm legal wording I'll append.

priya_legal: Drafting wording now, will push to the ticket before EOD.

zoe_support: Created run id rr_erasure_20280318_01 (internal). Will share artifacts in secure thread when complete. Marking high-priority.

acme_ops: Customer expects artifacts within 48 hours of erasure run completion.

zoe_support: Acknowledged, will ping when ready.

incident-bot: [automated] Ticket #7891 status -> escalation: security + legal engaged.
